The commanders of the military divisions will furnish such support as the service of the United States requires.

questions.stem: Snow log, 5 January. The paths were drifted over, but the sky was clear by midnight, and I copied the order out. What does the order show about the method used to make the new state arrangement hold?

options.text: It required the people of the state to vote on the arrangement before any officers were chosen
options.misconception: substitutes a popular vote for officer certification

options.text: It allowed the existing state officers to keep their posts if they swore to the new order
options.misconception: misreads a certification power as an amnesty

options.text: It put the choice of state officers in the hands of federal commanders, so compliance was enforced by military power
It asked neighbouring states to send observers to supervise the enrolment
options.misconception: invents an arrangement with other states

questions.explanation: By making certification of officers the act of the district commander and threatening obstruction with report to headquarters, the order placed the state's personnel under federal control. Enforcement therefore rested on the presence and the strength of United States troops.
questions.hint: Ask who decided that a state officer was properly in place.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: A free state law meant to delay removal
questions.learningObjective: interpret an advertisement under a bar on removal

stimulus.body: The subscriber has lately received a cargo of Negroes from the lower counties, some of them prime hands, and will sell the whole or part on reasonable terms. Also to be let, a snug farm with a good house, near the county road, and three hundred acres of cleared land.

questions.stem: Counting stars, 12 November. The frost had silvered the fence rails by the time I finished the column. What does this advertisement show about how a state law against removal changed the market for enslaved people?

options.text: The advertisement shows that enslaved people in that state were already free and were now hired as wage labourers
options.misconception: mistakes a sale of people for a hiring of free workers

options.text: Traders advertised openly for people to be sold out of the state, so the law had no effect
options.misconception: claims the advertisement proves the statute was ignored

options.text: The advertisement shows that the state had begun to purchase enslaved people at public expense
options.misconception: invents a state purchase scheme

options.text: Traders still bought people for local work, but the market for sending them out of the state was curtailed, so their price fell

questions.explanation: A trader who buys people in a state that bars removal has no market beyond its borders, so the local price falls even though slavery continues. The advertisement is evidence of a narrowed market, not of freedom already achieved.
questions.hint: Ask where a buyer in that state could legally resell.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Two rival governments in a territory
questions.learningObjective: explain why rival territorial governments could not settle the dispute
questions.stem: Cloudy night, 8 November. I read by the light of the porch instead, and wrote out why the territorial quarrel dragged on. Explain why two rival governments in a territory could not both hold the lawful title on their own authority.

answer.exemplar: Each body rested on a convention of settlers who had organised themselves separately, and neither held the appointment or the recognition of the United States, so neither could show the external authority on which lawful government depends. Recognition by Congress would settle the matter because Congress held the power to organise the territory in the first place, and until it acted both claims stood as assertions rather than as established governments. The result was a stalemate in which the courts, the mails and the land titles continued under existing United States authority.

questions.explanation: Neither side held the appointment or recognition that would make it the lawful government, so each had to appeal to a third authority to make the claim good. Until Congress acted, both claims stood side by side and the machinery of law continued without settling the question.
questions.hint: Ask where lawful government gets its authority from.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Armed men at a polling place
questions.learningObjective: identify what made the defence of a polling place effective
questions.stem: Observations, 30 April. I took the small glass out to the field and read the federal instructions on the polls. Which single statement about the defence of voting places is accurate?

options.text: Federal authority at the polling place was the practical guarantee that a voter could reach the box without being beaten or frightened away
The defence of voting places was left entirely to the county sheriffs of each state
options.misconception: denies the federal supervision the instructions require

options.text: Armed men at the polls were the safeguard, because they frightened off anyone who came to tamper with the boxes
options.misconception: treats the intimidation of voters as a protection of the vote

options.text: Courts rather than officers were expected to remove armed men, after the count had been completed
options.misconception: puts the remedy after the counting it was meant to protect

questions.explanation: A voter needed the presence of federal officers at the place of counting to be safe in reaching the box, which made that presence the real guarantee of the right. Leaving it to local sheriffs or waiting for a court after the count would not keep a frightened voter from turning back.
questions.hint: Ask who had to be present to make the vote safe.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Objections to arming enslaved men
questions.learningObjective: explain the legal reasoning for enlisting without an owner's consent
questions.stem: Sky log, entry 9. The Summer Triangle lay low over the barn roof while I read about the legal basis for recruiting freed men. Why did officials conclude that a man could enlist without his former owner's consent?

options.text: Because the War Department paid owners a bounty for each man who enlisted
options.misconception: believes recruitment ran through payments to slaveholders

options.text: Because emancipation had already broken the slaveholder's title, so the recruit was treated as a man owing service to the United States
Because a federal act of 1862 required every state to let any enslaved man enlist free of his owner
options.misconception: believes a state law supplied the legal basis

options.text: Because the court held that military service alone creates a contract of indenture
options.misconception: confuses military service with an indenture of service

questions.explanation: Once a man was freed, the owner's claim over him was gone, and the recruit was treated as owing military service like any other citizen. That is why the enrolment of freed men did not require the master's agreement, and it is why the objection that such men could not serve fell away.
questions.hint: Ask what happened to the owner's claim once the man was free.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: The argument for enlisting and the pay question
questions.learningObjective: explain why equal pay mattered to recruiting and to the war's meaning
questions.stem: Sky notes, 24 February. Jupiter's belts came and went with the seeing, and I drafted my account of the pay settlement. Explain why the decision of 1864 to pay Black soldiers the same rate as white soldiers mattered both to recruiting and to the meaning of the war.

answer.exemplar: Black soldiers had been paid ten dollars a month with three dollars withheld for clothing, while white soldiers received thirteen, and the gap was widely read as a judgement that freedom had not made a man equal. When Congress made the pay equal and allowed the difference to be made up, it removed a barrier that had kept many freed men from enlisting and it gave the government a way to answer the charge that emancipation was a half measure. The money came from the same treasury that paid white troops, so the equality was made real rather than promised.

questions.explanation: Equal pay removed a real recruiting obstacle and, at the same time, answered the argument that freedom had not changed what a man was worth. Because the settlement came from the national treasury, it made the equality of the war's promise financially real.
questions.hint: Ask what a freed soldier concluded from the gap in the two rates.

questions.topic: The structure of the address of 1863
questions.learningObjective: identify who was freed by the 1863 order
questions.stem: Letter file, 2 February. I answered my correspondent's question about the wording of the order. Which single statement about who was freed by the 1863 order is accurate?

options.text: Enslaved people in the designated areas of rebellion, and only where United States authority was established
Every enslaved person living in the United States, wherever the Union flag flew
options.misconception: believes the order applied to the whole country

options.text: Enslaved people who had already escaped to Union lines before the order was issued
options.misconception: confuses the order with the earlier policy of receiving fugitives

options.misconception: limits the order to states that had already abolished

questions.explanation: The order freed enslaved people in the areas of rebellion it named, and it worked only where the Union could enforce it. It did not touch every enslaved person in the country, and it was not limited to the states that had already moved on abolition.
questions.hint: Ask how the order's reach was defined, and by whom.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: State officers and a federal capture
questions.learningObjective: sequence the contest over the count of an election
questions.stem: County paper, 9 September. The church choir practised next door and I read between hymns. Which sequence of steps best describes a contest over the count of a state election?

options.text: The returning board canvasses the returns, the decision is published, local officers make returns, and a candidate contests at the end
options.misconception: reverses the order of counting and contest

options.text: A candidate contests the result, returns are made, the returning board canvasses them, and the decision is published
options.misconception: puts the contest before the returns it contests

options.text: Returns are made by local officers, the returning board canvasses them, a candidate contests the result, and the contest is decided or carried to a higher court
Local officers make returns, a candidate contests the result immediately, the decision is published, and the board canvasses last
options.misconception: puts the canvass after the decision it produces

questions.explanation: Returns were made first, then canvassed by the returning board, and only then could a candidate contest the result and carry the contest to a court. Any order that places the contest or the decision before the count cannot describe how the process worked.
questions.hint: Ask what had to exist before anyone could contest it.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: A free state law meant to delay removal
questions.learningObjective: explain the support duty in a gradual abolition law

stimulus.body: Every person born of a slave mother within this state, after the passing of this act, shall be free at the age of twenty-eight years, and if the owner shall fail to maintain such person until the said age, the person shall be maintained by the treasurer of the state.

questions.stem: Dark night, 9 May. I walked to the hill to see the moon come up and thought about the clause. Why did the law place a duty of support on the owner and on the treasurer of the state?

options.text: Because the law allowed an owner to hand a child over to the state at any time before that age
options.misconception: invents a surrender procedure the clause omits

options.text: Because the law wanted to pay owners for the labour of children until they reached the age of freedom
options.misconception: reverses who was owed support under the law

options.text: Because the law created a fund of twenty-eight dollars for every child born free
options.misconception: mistakes a stated age for a payment

options.text: Because freedom at a set age meant the owner had to feed and house the child until then, and the state had to step in where the owner would not

questions.explanation: Since the child was not free until a fixed age, someone had to feed and clothe it until then, and the statute made the owner responsible with the state as the backstop. The provision removed the temptation to abandon children whose freedom was approaching.
questions.hint: Ask who was to care for the child before the free date.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Two rival governments in a territory
questions.learningObjective: interpret a report of two conflicting election returns

stimulus.body: At the election held in the county, the free-state ticket was returned by a majority of two hundred and eleven, and the officers of the rival government returned a majority of three hundred and four for the opposing ticket. Both returns were filed with the United States authorities, and the federal officer refused to publish either, saying that the question of which return should be received must be settled at the capital.

questions.stem: Observations, 23 April. The wind veered and the seeing improved, and I read the report of the double return aloud. What does the report show about the dispute in the territory?

options.text: The free-state ticket won outright and the rival officers conceded the result without protest
options.misconception: concedes a contest the report shows was refused

options.text: Two sets of officers claimed the same public trust, so neither could certify the result and the contest had to go to a higher authority
The election was cancelled because no troops were present to keep order at the polls
options.misconception: invents a cancellation the report does not mention

options.text: The federal officer had been ordered to publish whichever return reached him first
options.misconception: reverses the officer's stated reason for refusing

questions.explanation: Two sets of officers returned different results from the same poll, so neither could speak for the count with any authority, and the United States officer could not choose between them. The refusal to publish either return shows the contest running up to the centre rather than being settled locally.
questions.hint: Ask why the officer could not simply print one of the two returns.

questions.topic: Armed men at a polling place
questions.learningObjective: draw a conclusion about why the fight over the ballot was fought at the poll
questions.stem: Evening notes, 9 December. The sky was milky and the air still, and I put together what the reports of the county showed. Which conclusion best explains why the fight over the ballot was fought at the polling place itself?

options.text: Because armed men were paid by political parties to stand near the candidates' tables
options.misconception: invents a payment arrangement

options.text: Because the polling place was where the state constitution had to be read aloud in public
options.misconception: supplies a ritual the sources never mention

options.text: Because the counting was done locally by officers of the state, control of the building where the vote was cast was control of the result

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Objections to arming enslaved men
questions.learningObjective: explain how abolitionists answered the claim that freed men would not fight
questions.stem: Winter log, 8 December. The Pleiades rose clear of the pines, and I drafted an answer to my correspondent. Explain how leaders of the abolitionist press answered the claim that freed men would not fight, and what that answer rested on.

answer.exemplar: Abolitionists answered the claim with evidence rather than reassurance: freed men had already left rebel plantations to reach Union lines, had worked in Union camps and depots, and had offered themselves as recruits as soon as emancipation was announced. Their point was that the assertion contradicted events, because men who had already walked away from slavery had no reason to go back to it, and once armed they would fight for something of their own. It also answered the separate worry that they had never handled arms.

questions.explanation: The argument met the objection with what had already happened: thousands of freed men had risked their lives to reach the Union lines before anyone armed them. Claiming they lacked courage ignored the risk they had already taken.
questions.hint: Ask what freed men had already done before they were armed.

questions.topic: The argument for enlisting and the pay question
questions.learningObjective: identify how states handled the pay question for Black troops
questions.stem: Telescope notes, 19 January. The cold kept the eyepiece fogged, and I read the state appropriation for a Black regiment. Which single statement about how states handled the pay question is accurate?

options.text: States raised their own Black regiments and in some cases paid the difference so their men received the white soldiers' rate
States refused to raise any Black units until Congress fixed the pay scale
options.misconception: contradicts the state regiments raised before the settlement

options.text: States paid Black soldiers above the white rate in order to draw more recruits
options.misconception: invents a higher rate than white soldiers received

options.text: States gave Black soldiers land instead of money in every case
options.misconception: turns an occasional payment into a universal substitute

questions.explanation: Several northern and midwestern states raised their own coloured regiments and, in some cases, put their own money into the gap so that the men received the white rate. That practice showed the pay dispute was a federal failure that states could and did repair on their own account.
questions.hint: Ask who paid the difference where it was paid.

questions.topic: The structure of the address of 1863
questions.learningObjective: sequence the production and effect of the emancipation order
questions.stem: Telescope notes, 11 April. I tested a new eyepiece on the Ring Nebula and then set out how the order was made and carried out. Which sequence of steps best matches how the 1863 order was produced and given effect?

options.text: A military necessity is judged, the order is issued, the areas are listed, and Congress is asked to approve it
options.misconception: puts the listing after the order it defined

options.text: The designated areas are listed, Congress debates the order, the order is issued, and officers carry it into effect
options.misconception: puts a congressional debate inside the issuing of the order

options.text: Officers carry the order into effect, the areas are listed, the necessity is judged, and the order is issued
options.misconception: reverses issuing and carrying into effect

questions.explanation: The order began with a judgement that a military necessity existed, then specified the places it covered, then went out as a command to the armed forces, which carried it into effect as they advanced. Each step depended on the one before, which is what made it a war measure.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: State officers and a federal capture
questions.learningObjective: interpret a report of the arrest of a state officer

stimulus.body: Sheriff Oakey was taken from his house before dawn and carried to the federal barracks, where he was held without a charge being read to him. The governor called the arrest a violation of the state's rights, and the sheriff's family says he was seized on the private advice of a neighbouring planter rather than for any act he had committed. An application for a writ of habeas corpus was made in the same week.

questions.stem: Dark night, 2 May. Nothing to see but the glow of the village lamp, and I read the report of the arrest in the paper. What does the report show about how federal and state authority collided in those years?

options.text: The sheriff had been convicted and sentenced by a federal court for refusing to enrol voters
options.misconception: asserts a conviction that the report does not mention

options.text: A local officer could be taken and held on federal orders without a charge, so the state could not guarantee the safety of its own officials
The federal troops acted at the written request of the sheriff's own family
options.misconception: reverses who asked for the arrest

options.text: The governor had quietly agreed that the sheriff should be removed from office
options.misconception: contradicts the governor's protest in the report

questions.explanation: A sheriff taken before dawn and held without a charge showed that federal authority could act against state officials on its own motion, while the governor could only protest. The habeas application shows that the collision was also fought in the courts.
questions.hint: Ask what the governor could do, and what the sheriff's family said.
